title: A systematic review of non-contact medical IoT systems for physiological biomarker monitoring
authors: Bithi Banik; Saptanil Ghose; Ahnaf Hasnain Nahiun; Yuan Lin; Andrii Shalaginov; Debasish Ghose
abstract: Introduction Non-contact medical Internet of Things systems measure physiological biomarkers such as heart rate (HR), respiration rate (RR), temperature, oxygen saturation (SpO₂), and blood pressure (BP) without physical contact with the patient. These systems combine sensing modalities including cameras, radar, Wi-Fi, acoustic, and infrared sensors with signal processing and learning algorithms to deliver comfortable, non-invasive monitoring. Prior reviews have largely examined individual sensing modalities or signal processing techniques in isolation, leaving cross-modality system architecture and privacy-preserving design underexamined. Methods We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA guidelines and analyzed 88 recent studies of non-contact monitoring systems. Studies were characterized by sensing modality, system architecture, target physiological parameter, validation setting, and reported performance. We additionally assessed each study for methodological quality and examined the extent to which privacy-preserving mechanisms were incorporated into system design. Results Radar and vision-based systems dominate the corpus, together accounting for approximately three-quarters of included studies, while sound, Wi-Fi, embedded sensor, and mixed-modality designs remain at an earlier stage of validation. Research effort is heavily concentrated on two parameters: RR appears in 83% of studies and HR in 67%, while no other parameter exceeds 11%. BP, SpO₂, and temperature therefore remain largely unaddressed by contactless methods. Heterogeneous reporting metrics across studies prevent direct statistical comparison of performance between modalities. Discussion The findings indicate that modality selection should be driven by deployment context rather than headline accuracy. Radar suits wards and intensive care units where patients are covered or moving, vision and sound suit structured clinical spaces with stable conditions, embedded sensor designs suit eldercare beds and chairs, and mixed radar and vision systems suit precision-critical settings such as neonatal and postoperative monitoring. Persistent challenges include signal reliability in uncontrolled environments, limited benchmarking due to the absence of standardized datasets, privacy and ethical concerns, and poor integration with existing healthcare infrastructure. Building on these insights, we propose a conceptual federated, edge-based learning framework, presented as a design proposal for future implementation rather than a validated system, and outline research directions to accelerate clinical translation.

title: Application of LLM combined with knowledge base in improving C-TIRADS grading of thyroid nodules
authors: Qian Qu; Hanwen Bi; Xiaofei Yu; Rui Zhou; Zhen Liu; Tengteng Hao
abstract: Objective This study used the unified text-based grading results of senior sonographers as the primary reference (this text benchmark is not pathological diagnostic gold standard) to evaluate the concordance of text-derived C-TIRADS grades assigned by six large language models (LLMs), with and without FastGPT Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) knowledge base assistance. Our primary endpoint was the concordance between grading and physician consensus—a measure fundamentally distinct from pathological diagnostic accuracy. Only a small subgroup with pathological confirmation was used for a supplementary exploratory analysis of the correlation between model risk stratification and pathological benign or malignant findings. Methods Six LLMs were configured using the C-TIRADS criteria. A FastGPT knowledge base was built from 11,489 thyroid ultrasound records collected at Yantai Yuhuangding Hospital between 2022 and 2023. Cases were assigned to manual, LLM, and knowledge-base-augmented LLM groups. C-TIRADS grading concordance with expert ultrasound consensus, and grading speed were assessed. A subgroup of 62 pathologically confirmed nodules was used for supplementary exploratory analysis. AUC, sensitivity, specificity, PPV, NPV and Mantel-Haenszel linear trend χ2 were computed to examine the alignment of model C-TIRADS risk tiers with pathological benign and malignant findings. Results Among the standalone LLMs, DeepSeek-V3 achieved the highest numerical grading concordance (81.14%). Following the integration of the RAG knowledge base, overall grading consistency improved significantly ( P < 0.001), with Doubao-pro-128k demonstrating the highest overall concordance at 89.04%. Concordance increased significantly for C-TIRADS Categories 1 and 3 ( P = 0.027 and P < 0.001, respectively), increased numerically for Category 2 ( P = 0.596), and decreased numerically for borderline Category 4A ( P = 0.106). The average concordance across all categories rose significantly from 70.39% to 79.75% ( P < 0.001). The knowledge-augmented Doubao-pro-128k model exhibited excellent inter-rater agreement ( linear-weighted Kappa>0.8, Bonferroni-corrected P<0.006 ). The average single-case grading duration of all 12 AI risk tiering pipelines (6 LLMs with/without knowledge base) was 1.30 s, which was 15 times faster than manual grading (19.25 s). Stratified trend and ROC analyses were performed on 62 thyroid nodules with pathological outcomes. Within this small-sample exploratory pathological subgroup, the Doubao-pro-128k integrated with knowledge base established a significantly ascending malignant risk gradient, achieving an AUC of 0.783 (95% CI : 0.635, 0.932) for distinguishing benign from malignant lesions. In comparison, knowledge-enhanced Doubao-pro-128k exhibited a trend toward better matching trend with pathological malignancy distribution and numerically the highest positive Youden index of 0.277 (95% CI : 0.071, 0.482). Conclusion Doubao-pro-128k integrated with knowledge base accelerated text grading and improved overall sonographer concordance; category-specific concordance increased significantly for C-TIRADS 1 and 3, increased numerically for Category 2, and declined numerically without statistical significance for borderline C-TIRADS 4A, indicating that these ambiguous nodules require further optimization. Exploratory pathological analysis revealed variable model-pathology alignment at the C-TIRADS ≥ 4A cutoff: DeepSeek-V3 integrated with knowledge base produced a negative Youden index, while Doubao-pro-128k integrated with knowledge base showed a tentative trend toward better reflected pathological malignancy gradients.

title: Acronyms and Abbreviations in Modern English Language
authors: Aynur Afsar Guliyeva
abstract: Language is constantly evolving in response to the needs of its users. In English, numerous concepts are often conveyed through phrases or compound words, as such expressions enable a precise and comprehensive representation of the essential and sufficient features of each concept. Due to the considerable length of some terms, it is sometimes necessary to apply various methods of shortening. One of the most prominent changes in contemporary language use is the shortening or clipping of words and phrases. This process, referred to in linguistics as word shortening, plays a significant role in both spoken and written communication. People shorten words to save time, minimize effort, and adapt language to modern forms of interaction such as messaging and social media. Although shortening is often linked to informal language, it is also commonly found in academic, professional, and technical contexts. Although word formation in English is an area or a part of considerable interest in linguistic studies, it is regarded as a controversial field due to its complex nature.

title: Spatiotemporal differentiation and determinants of abandoned farmland utilization in the Yangtze River Economic Belt
authors: Zhe Zhu; Shiwen Chen; Leyi Shao; Ping Li; Heran Zou; Yilong Sheng
venue: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change
abstract: As a stabilizer safeguarding China’s food security, the Yangtze River Economic Belt is troubled by farmland abandonment and inefficient utilization of abandoned farmland. Therefore, clarifying the spatiotemporal differentiation and determinants of abandoned farmland utilization is critical to addressing challenges in cultivated land protection. Based on the China Land Cover Dataset (CLCD), this study adopts land-use trajectory analysis, kernel density analysis, and spatial autocorrelation analysis to explore core issues of abandoned farmland utilization from three dimensions: scale, efficiency and stability. The results show that: (1) Since 2022, abandoned farmland utilization policies have raised the annual utilization rate by an average of 2.5 percentage points. Historical abandoned land stocks are absorbed evenly each year, shifting governance from clearing accumulated abandoned land arrears to regularly controlling newly abandoned farmland. (2) Abandoned farmland utilization shows a striking west-high and east-low spatial agglomeration gradient: HH clusters distribute in the upper reaches and LL clusters in the lower reaches, with the upper and middle reaches achieving a 10-percentage-point 4-year growth in utilization rates. Utilization stability follows the middle reaches (91.12%), upper reaches (90.28%), and lower reaches (85.36%). (3) Natural geography, economic levels, labor composition and institutional policies cause these disparities. This research provides theoretical and practical support for differentiated regional governance of abandoned farmland and consolidated national food security.

title: ГРАМАТИЧНІ ЗАСОБИ ВИРАЖЕННЯ ПРИПУЩЕННЯ В ЯПОНСЬКІЙ МОВІ
authors: Olga Gorodyska
abstract: У статті досліджено граматичні засоби вираження припущення в сучасній японській мові в межах категорії епіс- темічної модальності. Актуальність дослідження зумовлена наявністю в японській мові розгалуженої системи гра- матичних конструкцій, за допомогою яких мовець передає різні типи неповної впевненості щодо достовірності пові- домлюваної інформації. До таких значень належать власне припущення, прогнозування, вираження можливості, високого ступеня переконаності, логічного висновку, а також висновку, сформованого на підставі безпосередньо спостережуваних ознак або інформації, отриманої з непрямих джерел. Матеріалом дослідження слугують основні модальні конструкції сучасної японської мови: だろう/でしょう, かもしれない, にちがいない, はずだ, ようだ, みたいだ, らしい та そうだ. У статті здійснено систематизацію зазначених граматичних засобів та визначено їхні функціонально-семантичні особливості в системі японської епістемічної модальності.У процесі дослідження використано описовий, семантич- ний і зіставний методи аналізу, що дають змогу встановити специфіку функціонування окремих модальних форм та визначити критерії їх розрізнення. З’ясовано, що відмінності між досліджуваними конструкціями визначаються не лише ступенем впевненості мовця у достовірності висловлення, а й характером інформаційної основи, на якій ґрунтується відповідне судження. З’ясовано, що だろう/でしょう переважно виражає припущення або прогноз щодо можливої ситуації; かもしれない позначає можливість реалізації певного сценарію; にちがいない передає високий ступінь переконано- сті мовця; はずだ пов’язане з логічно очікуваним результатом, який випливає з певних передумов, правил або відо- мих обставин. Особливу увагу приділено конструкціям ようだ, みたいだ, らしい та そうだ, функціонування яких тісно пов’язане з категорією доказовості та способом отримання інформації. Доведено, що ようだ виражає висно- вок, сформований на основі певних ознак або фактів, みたいだ функціонує переважно в розмовному мовленні та є близькою за значенням конструкцією, тоді як らしい може ґрунтуватися на непрямій інформації або сукупності наявних фактів. Окремо розрізнено два функціонально різні типи そうだ: конструкцію, що виражає припущення на основі безпосередньо сприйнятих зовнішніх ознак, та конструкцію зі значенням передавання інформації, отриманої від іншого джерела. Наукова новизна дослідження полягає у комплексній систематизації граматичних засобів вираження припу- щення за двома взаємопов’язаними параметрами: ступенем епістемічної впевненості та типом інформаційної основи судження. Такий підхід дає змогу пояснити відмінності між формами, які в українській мові нерідко передаються одна- ковими або близькими за значенням відповідниками, зокрема словами «мабуть», «можливо», «схоже», «напевно». Практичне значення отриманих результатів полягає у можливості їх використання під час викладання японської мови, розроблення навчальних матеріалів, а також у перекладацькій практиці, де правильний вибір відповідника залежить не лише від загального значення припущення, а й від способу формування висновку та епістемічної позиції мовця.

title: "COMMUNICATIVE AND PRAGMATIC STRATEGIES OF ONOMATOPOEIC UNITS IN ENGLISH AND UZBEK DIALOGIC SPEECH"
authors: Kayumova Ozoda Baxrom qizi; Worldly Knowledge Publishing Centre
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: This article examines the communicative and pragmatic functions of onomatopoeic units in English and Uzbek dialogic speech. The study focuses on the ways in which sound-imitative expressions contribute to the organization of interaction, the transmission of emotions, the expression of attitudes, the management of conversational turns, and the achievement of communicative intentions. Particular attention is paid to the relationship between the phonetic form of onomatopoeic units and their contextual pragmatic meanings. The research adopts a comparative descriptive approach, combining contextual, functional-semantic, and pragmatic analysis. Illustrative examples from English and Uzbek are used to identify similarities and differences in the use of sound-imitative expressions in dialogue. The analysis suggests that onomatopoeic units can perform several communicative functions simultaneously, including sound representation, emotional intensification, evaluative expression, attention management, and the dramatization of conversational events. Their pragmatic interpretation depends not only on their lexical meaning but also on intonation, repetition, conversational position, and the relationship between interlocutors. The study highlights the importance of distinguishing cross-linguistic functional similarities from language-specific forms and cultural conventions.

title: Alfalfa-Yolo: a boundary-aware lightweight framework for real-time weed detection in alfalfa fields
authors: Jingyi Wang; Kai Li; Tao Zhou; Yuanjun Xu; Yiwen Gao; Changzhong Li; Yanhua Zhao
abstract: Accurate weed detection in alfalfa fields is hindered by morphological similarity between crops and weeds at the seedling stage, substantial scale variation across weed targets, and degradation of fine spatial information during feature resampling. To address these challenges, Alfalfa-Yolo is proposed as a boundary-aware compact detection framework integrating three complementary components. The Edge-Perception Global Transfer Network (EPGTNet) uses bidirectional Sobel responses and cross-layer transmission to preserve edge-related high-frequency cues in deeper semantic features. The Multi-Scale Adaptive Feature Pyramid Network (MSAFPN) replaces static concatenation with attention-guided aggregation to adaptively regulate multi-scale contributions. The Enhanced Channel Shuffle Upsampling Module (ECSM) combines depthwise convolution, channel shuffle, and spatial shift to enhance local spatial representation after upsampling. On the self-constructed alfalfa-field dataset comprising 1,100 independent original field images, Alfalfa-Yolo achieves 77.6% mAP@0.5 and 55.9% mAP@0.5:0.95 with 2.67 M parameters. Independent-dataset benchmarking on CottonWeedDet12 and ImageWeeds confirms that the architecture remains competitive after target-dataset retraining, while a separate zero-shot cross-dataset protocol directly evaluates transfer without target-domain training. Deployment tests on NVIDIA RTX 4090, NVIDIA Orin NX, and RK3588 further characterize the accuracy-efficiency trade-off under different hardware and quantization settings. These results indicate that Alfalfa-Yolo provides a compact and practically deployable solution for real-time weed localization in alfalfa fields.

title: Towards Early and Accurate Disease Detection Through Multimodal Predictive Modeling: Fusion of Electronic Health Records, Medical Imaging, And Omics Data Using Interpretable Machine Learning.
authors: Muhammad Ahsan Hayat; Jahangir Baig; Shayan Ahmed; Ahmed Faraz Ayubi
abstract: Early detection of disease is a cornerstone for improving patient outcomes, reducing costs, and enabling preventative interventions. Traditional predictive models often rely on a single type of data (e.g., imaging, clinical labs, or genomics). However, human health is inherently multimodal, involving a variety of data sources such as electronic health records (EHRs), medical imaging, wearable sensor data, genomics, and clinical notes. Integrating these heterogeneous modalities into unified predictive modelsoffers a path to richer, more accurate, and more robust disease detection. In this paper, we present a comprehensive survey of methods in multimodal predictive modeling for early disease detection, illustrate architectural patterns and fusion strategies, discuss challenges (e.g. missing modalities, interpretability, generalizability, bias), and highlight promising directions. We also propose a reference architecture for developing such systems and suggest evaluation best practices.

title: Agentic code modernization
authors: Peter F. Peterson; Addi Malviya Thakur
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Software rots. Between refactors for new features, bug fixes, the continual march of cybersecurity advisories, and the slow drift of dependencies toward end-of-life, code must change or cease to exist. The simple act of keeping up can be overwhelming for research software engineers tasked with maintaining long-lived scientific codebases. To address this maintenance burden, the community has developed a vibrant ecosystem of language- and framework-specific tools, such as Dependabot for dependency bumps [1], Clang-Tidy for C++ static analysis [2], and Python Refurb for idiom modernization [3], alongside a host of similar utilities. These tools, while monumental in their contribution, are necessarily limited in scope: they encode a fixed catalog of transformations, they tend to operate on a single file or a single dependency at a time, and they presumably cannot reason about the broader architectural or semantic consequences of a change. More recently, agentic AI systems have arrived. Unlike single-shot code completion, agentic systems can read across a repository, run tests, observe failures, and iterate, and these behaviors, in principle, may enable a different class of modernization task. In this talk, we present concrete examples of modernizing Mantid [4], a more than 20-year-old C++ and Python project with roughly two million lines of code. We attempted to leverage agentic AI to perform maintenance work and modernization work on research software. Changes proposed by the agents were validated against the project's existing automated test suite and reviewed by human maintainers before merging. By exploring successes and failures, the presentation will improve attendees' understanding of when, and with what guardrails, to use AI to assist in modernizing their code. References Dependabot. title: Genotype-specific molecular and functional trajectories in NGLY1 deficiency: a comparative multi-omics study of patient-derived iPSC neurons
authors: Soukaina Amniouel; Zeenat A. Shyr; William F. Borschel; Mitali Arun Tambe; Atena Farkhondeh; Wei Zheng
venue: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
abstract: Background NGLY1 deficiency is an ultra-rare congenital disorder of deglycosylation with prominent neurodevelopmental impairment and marked allelic heterogeneity. Prior human neuronal models have characterized NGLY1 loss largely within single genetic backgrounds, leaving open whether distinct patient genotypes converge on a shared molecular state or follow divergent routes. Because clinical presentations overlap across genotypes, resolving this question requires a direct, within-system comparison of multiple genotypes rather than characterization of any single line. Methods We generated iPSC-derived glutamatergic neurons from three patients carrying distinct biallelic NGLY1 genotypes (R401X/R401X, Q208X/G310G, L318P/R390P) and two healthy controls, and profiled them head-to-head using matched transcriptomics and proteomics at day 28, RNA to protein concordance and differential exon usage analysis, pathway and phenotype network integration, and longitudinal multielectrode array (MEA) recordings during early network maturation. Results Across both molecular layers, samples segregated strongly by genotype rather than forming a unified disease signature. Differential expression revealed pronounced between-genotype heterogeneity with only a small shared molecular core. RNA to protein concordance was moderate and genotype-dependent, and differential exon usage was enriched among discordant genes in a mutation-dependent manner, implicating splicing-level regulation in the transcript to protein divergence. Integrated networks linked genotype-specific concordant changes to synaptic signaling, calcium handling, metabolism, and extracellular matrix remodeling, and connected them to overlapping clinical phenotypes through distinct molecular routes. MEA recordings showed delayed maturation and genotype-dependent shifts in network excitability, with functional clustering that mirrored the molecular separation. Conclusion Distinct NGLY1 genotypes produce divergent molecular and functional trajectories that converge on impaired network maturation through non-identical routes. These findings reframe NGLY1 deficiency as a set of genotype-specific molecular states rather than a single phenotype, with direct implications for mechanistic subgrouping and the design of preclinical models and validation studies.

title: Legal Nugget Extraction for Granular Retrieval over Long Jurisprudential Texts
authors: Lucas Pereira; Erick de Brito; Roberto Lotufo; Jayr Pereira
abstract: Legal retrieval over jurisprudential collections is challenging because court decisions are long, heterogeneous documents whose relevant legal thesis may occupy only a small portion of the text. This paper asks whether legal nuggets, defined as short and self-contained legal theses extracted from source documents, can improve dense retrieval over Brazilian legal collections. We propose a pipeline that extracts nuggets from each document, indexes them with embeddings, retrieves nugget-level evidence, and aggregates the retrieved nuggets back to document-level rankings. We evaluate this approach on four Portuguese legal retrieval benchmarks from the JUA ecosystem, reporting NDCG@10, MAP@10, and MRR@10. Nugget retrieval substantially improves the two jurisprudential datasets: on JUA-Juris, NDCG@10 increases from 0.10265 to 0.20461, and on JurisTCU from 0.20898 to 0.32696. However, it underperforms full-document retrieval on NormasTCU and BR-TaxQA, and an embedding-model ablation shows that strong domain-adapted retrievers can remain better in the full-document setting. The results demonstrate that legal nuggets can be useful for jurisprudence search, especially when queries are formulated as legal theses, but they may not transfer equally well to other legal retrieval scenarios.

title: Does SRL Pave the Road to Explainable Reasoning? Lessons Learned from an Implementer's Perspective
authors: Lander Maes; Bryan-Elliott Tam; Jitse De Smet; Jos De Roo; Pieter Colpaert; Ruben Taelman
abstract: The Shape Rules Language (SRL) Working Draft defines how to derive new RDF triples from an RDF graph using inference rules. Each rule matches graph patterns and instantiates triple templates whose output feeds into validation pipelines, SPARQL queries, or further inference. RDF reasoning has traditionally relied on fixed entailment regimes (RDFS, OWL), rule-based ad-hoc languages such as N3, or other implementation-specific solutions without a shared standard. SRL introduces user-defined production rules with a defined grammar, dependency analysis, execution ordering, and termination guarantees. However, no authoritative implementation exists, leaving practitioners with little guidance on how to build a conformant engine or on what problems the language can solve. We implemented two SRL engines and evaluated both on classical RDF reasoning tasks for soundness, completeness, and speed. The first reuses an existing SPARQL query engine and its query parser; the second is a dedicated engine. The SPARQL-based engine reused an existing modular parser for query construction and SPARQL CONSTRUCT for triple production, reducing engine-specific work. The dedicated engine was two to six times faster, the gap widening as rule sets grow. Both engines were validated against the SRL conformance test suite, supplemented by additional use-case-driven tests. A usable SRL engine can be built inexpensively on top of a SPARQL engine, with a moderate speed trade-off that a dedicated implementation recovers. Despite the specification's immaturity, the language already supports practically useful reasoning tasks.

title: Canadian Parliament Open Data and Embedded Vector Knowledge Base: InsightToast (UIST '26) Supplemental Dataset
authors: Mohammad Abolnejadian; Matthew Brehmer
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Canadian Parliament Open Data and Embedded Vector Knowledge Base: InsightToast (UIST '26) Supplemental Dataset 📄 Paper: https://doi.org/10.1145/3830398.3830522💻 Code: https://github.com/ubixgroup/InsightToast Supplemental dataset for the paper: InsightToast: Proactive Information Retrieval & Glanceable Visualization in the Side Channel of Data-Rich Meetings Mohammad Abolnejadian and Matthew Brehmer. Proceedings of the 39th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology (UIST '26). DOI: 10.1145/3830398.3830522 This dataset provides a collection of 43,878 open legislative records from the Canadian House of Commons, spanning 1994 to 2025, covering document types such as debates (Hansard), legislative bills, committee reports, petitions, recorded votes, order papers, and Library of Parliament research publications. It is released at three stages of the same pipeline: the raw collected documents, a processed corpus that has been passed through an ETL pipeline and chunked for use in a retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) pipeline, and an embedded, pre-indexed vector store built from that processed corpus. The dataset supports the development and user study of the InsightToast project. The embedded form can be placed directly into the project's codebase, open sourced at https://github.com/ubixgroup/InsightToast, where it serves as the knowledge base when InsightToast operates as a proactive side-channel assistant in policy discussion meetings. Usage in the InsightToast Backend Only qdrant_storage.tar.gz is required to run the backend. Extract it into the root of the InsightToast project, so that qdrant_storage/ sits alongside docker-compose.yml, and start the services: tar -xzf qdrant_storage.tar.gz -C /path/to/InsightToast/ cd /path/to/InsightToast docker compose up --build -d Contents File What it is Approx. size parliament_data.tar.gz Raw source corpus of 43,878 parliamentary records, as 57,124 files (.txt + .pdf) 8.1 GB compressed / 11 GB extracted parliament_data_processed.tar.gz Processed corpus: the same records cleaned, normalized, and chunked into RAG-ready JSON 2.1 GB compressed / 9.1 GB extracted qdrant_storage.tar.gz Pre-indexed Qdrant vector store, ready to mount as the knowledge base 21 GB compressed / 27 GB extracted parliament_data.STRUCTURE.txt Manifest of the raw corpus, viewable without downloading the archive small parliament_data_processed.STRUCTURE.txt Manifest of the processed corpus small qdrant_storage.STRUCTURE.txt Manifest of the vector store small SHA256SUMS.txt SHA-256 checksums for the three archives small Verify the archives after download: sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS.txt Source Corpus: Raw Parliamentary Documents parliament_data.tar.gz contains open legislative documents collected across the range of record types produced by the Canadian House of Commons and the Library of Parliament, including the proceedings of debate, the texts of bills as tabled, the reports of standing committees, the petitions presented to the House, and the recorded outcomes of divisions. The documents were assembled from three public sources: the House of Commons (ourcommons.ca, including the Legislative Information service, LEGISinfo), the Library of Parliament of Canada (parl-gc.primo.exlibrisgroup.com), and the independent open-data mirror openparliament.ca. No private, personal, or access-restricted material is included; Member of Parliament profiles contain only information published in an official public capacity. Total: 43,878 parliamentary records, distributed across 57,124 files (43,634 .txt + 13,490 .pdf). Each record is provided as extracted plain text, with the source PDF alongside it under the same basename where one exists, so records that carry both formats account for two files. Temporal coverage: documents span the 35th through 45th Parliaments. Debates run from 1994-01-17 to 2025-10-10; coverage of the other record types varies by type. Languages: the source records are bilingual (English and French), as published by Parliament. Filename conventions: debates use sitting dates (YYYY-MM-DD- .txt); bills, journals, order papers, and votes use - - (for example, 37-1-C-10); petitions and Library of Parliament publications use slugified titles. Category Files Description debates/ 18,347 House of Commons debates (Hansard transcripts), one file per sitting day bills/ 10,561 Legislative bills, full text plus the original tabled PDF journals/ 7,038 Official Journals of the House (daily record of decisions) petitions/ 6,093 e-Petitions and paper petitions presented to the House votes/ 4,521 Recorded division and vote results order-papers/ 4,228 Order Paper and Notice Paper (daily agenda) library/ 2,202 Library of Parliament publications and tabled agreements committee-reports/ 1,577 Standing and joint committee reports, grouped into 27 committee subfolders politicians/ 1,319 Member of Parliament profiles research/ 1,210 Library of Parliament research and HillNotes publications committees/ 28 Committee mandate and description summaries Total 57,124 See parliament_data.STRUCTURE.txt for the full breakdown, including all committee subfolders. Processed Corpus: Cleaned and Chunked Records parliament_data_processed.tar.gz contains the same corpus after the ETL pipeline that turns each document into retrievable units. Documents are parsed from their metadata header and routed by document_type. Bilingual records are language-identified with langdetect and reduced to their English content by an LLM pass. PDFs are structurally partitioned with unstructured's partition_pdf into text, table, and image elements; table elements are linearized into prose by an LLM, and salient figures are captioned, written to images/, and linked from their chunk via has_images. Records whose content is inherently tabular, namely recorded votes, petitions, and Member profiles, are rendered into natural-language narratives to keep them semantically retrievable rather than reducing to fields. Type-specific pre-segmentation then splits debates on speaker turns, preserving the speaker, section, and timestamp, before every stream passes through a RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter (1,000 characters, 200 overlap); each resulting chunk is tagged with its content_type (text, table, or image) and its provenance. The output is one JSON document per record, holding the record's metadata and its ordered list of chunks: { "metadata": { "document_type": "debate", "session": "35-1", "date": "1994-01-17", "language": "en", "source_file": "debates/1994-01-17-1.txt", "source_url": "...", "total_chunks": 51 }, "chunks": [ { "chunk_id": 0, "content": "...", "metadata": { "speaker": "...", "section": "...", "content_type": "text", "has_images": false } } ] } Volume: 42,014 JSON records and 2,170 extracted images, totaling 6,379,732 chunks, which is the set embedded into the knowledge base below. Traceability: every record's metadata.source_file links back to its file in the raw corpus. Coverage: most record types are processed in full; committee-report and library are present as subsets of the raw corpus. See parliament_data_processed.STRUCTURE.txt for per-category counts. Indexed Knowledge Base qdrant_storage.tar.gz contains the processed corpus above embedded and indexed into Qdrant, ready to serve as the retrieval backend with no further processing. Qdrant version: built with qdrant/qdrant:v1.13.6. Qdrant's on-disk format is version-specific, so load this snapshot with the same or a compatible version to avoid migration issues. title: Information need themes and their dynamics among people living with HIV/AIDS: an illness journey perspective
authors: Ne Cai; Zhengbiao Han; Preben Hansen
abstract: Introduction. It is crucial to identify the thematic information needs expressed by people living with HIV/AIDS across media platforms, and to analyse their dynamic evolution through different disease stages to facilitate targeted informational provision. Method. Information need statements from people living with HIV/AIDS were collected (2022–2024) from Little Red Book, Baidu Knows, Haodf.com, and the Zhi Ai Jiayuan forum. Analysis. BERTopic and dynamic topic modelling were used to identify themes, compare platform differences, and trace longitudinal changes over time. Results. Information need themes differed significantly across platforms. On Little Red Book, individuals tended to emphasise information needs related to emotional support and social relationship adjustment; on Baidu Knows, they focused on disease management and maintaining life balance; on Haodf.com, they prioritised professional medical advice, and on the Zhi Ai Jiayuan forum, they sought comprehensive HIV-related information together with social support. The study also found dynamic changes in thematic information needs. During the early stage of HIV infection (stage I), individuals sought emotional support and foundational disease information. During the middle stage (stage II), their information needs diversified to include treatment strategies and family support. During the Advancing to AIDS (stage III), information needs became more specialised, emphasising treatment outcomes and complication management. Conclusion. Both platform context and disease stage shape the expression of individuals’ information needs. The findings underscore the value of platform- and stage-tailored information services that evolve from psychosocial reassurance to complex clinical guidance.

title: Dynamic adaptation of attentional control across bilingual interactional contexts
authors: Min Li; Xiangyu Shi; Qinghong Xu; Jie Li
abstract: Background/objectives Bilingual experience is thought to shape cognitive control via adaptive attentional reorganization, yet the neural mechanisms by which different interactional contexts dynamically modulate attentional control remain unclear. This study used EEG to examine how Chinese monolingual, English monolingual, bilingual, and voluntary naming contexts influence attentional control in Chinese–English bilinguals. Methods Thirty-five bilinguals completed picture-naming tasks in different contexts, followed by an antisaccade task with concurrent EEG. We analyzed reaction time, ERPs, frontal and parietal delta/theta power, and frontoparietal functional connectivity (wPLI). Results Bilingual and voluntary naming contexts shortened antisaccade reaction times (all p < 0.01). No significant main effect of context was found on N2 amplitudes ( p = 0.615). Both contexts reduced parietal delta and theta power relative to the English monolingual context (all p < 0.05). Exploratory connectivity analysis initially suggested bilingual-context effects, but this finding did not survive homologous ROI validation. These preliminary sensor-level findings await validation by source-localized EEG or fMRI. Conclusions These findings suggest that bilingual and voluntary naming contexts may facilitate attentional control through adaptive reorganization of the attentional system rather than through enhancing a specific inhibitory process. This pattern is consistent with the adaptationist perspective on bilingual cognition and provides preliminary neural evidence for the language mode theory.

title: Measuring a scaffold from inside: an operator-authored self-measurement harness for a constitutional runtime over a hosted language model
authors: Richard Dobson
abstract: Interactive intelligent systems constructed over hosted large language models cannot retrain the substrate on which they depend, and so their designers enforce a named epistemology at the surrounding scaffold layer. A difficulty follows that has received little methodological attention: when quality regresses, the regression frequently belongs to the scaffold rather than the substrate, and identifying it requires instruments that measure the scaffold itself rather than the model beneath it. This article reports one such instrument set, added to a live constitutional runtime between 17 and 18 July 2026 and extended with a production drift observer on 19 August 2026, and situates it as a reusable design pattern. The layer comprises six components—operator-authored adversarial batteries held as versioned regression fixtures, deterministic pattern screens encoding named defects, an emission quarantine that retains failure evidence as a first-class object, an instrument-health monitor issuing autonomous handoffs, continuous-integration delivery tripwires, and an observe-only production drift detector that accumulates a hand-labelling corpus from live traffic without altering any replies. Eight falsifiable harness predictions are stated (H1 through H8), each named against a specific runtime carrier—a code path, a database table, or a typed field—and each paired with an explicit falsification condition; their relationship to the eight pre-registered outcome predictions (F1 through F8) of a companion architecture paper is stated in a dedicated reconciliation section, since the harness reported here is the instrument set on which those outcome predictions depend. Of the eight, five (H1, H2, H3, H5, H7) carry dated on-platform observations and are reported in a dedicated observed subsection; three (H4, H6, H8) are prospective—predictions about experiments that have not yet occurred—and are reported separately under that label, so that no reader mistakes the distribution of evidence. The predictions are offered for adversarial replication under an honest empirical frame rather than as settled results: the batteries were authored by the platform’s operator, classification is not independent, and the number of platforms studied is one. The discussion states a narrow priority claim, distinguishes the enforcement point of composition-time assertion from adjacent techniques, extends the pattern to the governance of learning loops—a scaffold that adapts must be measured by the same discipline that measures a scaffold that enforces—and argues that the interaction properties a reader encounters, an observation lock and per-turn provenance grounding, become testable precisely because they are structurally enforced.
